title: The Sound of a Black Hole
sources: NASA Chandra 'A Universe of Sound' - Perseus (chandra.si.edu/sound/perseus.html): ripples ~57 octaves below middle C; audio scaled up 57-58 octaves
hedge_notes: Say 'roughly 240 million light years' - distance came from a secondary source, not a NASA page
Always call it sonification; the raw note is not audible

segments.label: SPACE HUMS
segments.text: Space is silent. But one black hole is humming.
segments.prompt: a black hole with glowing accretion disk in deep space

segments.label: 240M LIGHT YEARS
segments.text: It sits in the Perseus galaxy cluster, roughly two hundred and forty million light years away.
segments.prompt: a swirling spiral galaxy in deep space

segments.label: HOT GAS
segments.text: Between those galaxies is hot gas, and hot gas can carry pressure waves, like sound.
segments.prompt: colorful glowing nebula gas clouds in space

segments.label: CHANDRA
segments.text: NASA's Chandra X-ray telescope found ripples in that gas, stirred up by the black hole at the center.
segments.prompt: the Chandra X-ray space telescope orbiting Earth, solar panels, deep space, photorealistic

segments.label: 57 OCTAVES
segments.text: Those ripples are a note about fifty-seven octaves below middle C. Far too deep for any human ear.
segments.prompt: glowing concentric ripples of pressure waves spreading through a dark cloud of hot gas in space

segments.label: SONIFICATION
segments.text: So scientists shifted the pitch way up, into the range we can hear. That process is called sonification.
segments.prompt: audio waveform visualizer glowing on dark background

segments.label: REAL DATA
segments.text: It is real data, translated into sound.
segments.prompt: a field of stars across the universe

segments.label: YOUR GUESS?
segments.text: What do you think a black hole sounds like?
segments.prompt: an astronaut silhouette looking into deep space
